messages:
incidents-bot: URGENT: GPU pool eu-west-1-a is at 98% utilization, queue growth sustained > 18m, token throttle triggered. Paging on-call @maya. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1905123456 :rotating_light:

maya: I'm on it. seeing increased 5xx and queue latency. Dashboard shows queue length ~32k, avg wait 4.2s, p95 latency jumping.

samir: autoscaler logs show repeated failures when attempting to add nodes: `Error: quotaExceeded` then `scaleLimitReached`. It tried 3 times in 10m.

liam: fyi — we pushed model v5 canary to a subset of traffic ~2h before this. Early telemetry shows median request tokens went from ~512 -> ~1800 for v5. KV-cache warmup traffic is hammering GPU memory and slowing throughput; that increases per-request GPU time.

maya: that explains sudden jump. are the failing autoscale events because of cloud project quota or our per-customer pool cap?

samir: looks like both. cloud quota is hitting a soft limit for GPU quota (region), and our pool config has `max_pools: 10` per cluster; pools are full.

jess: any idea which customers are affected? is this a broad degradation or canary-only?

support-anna: support queue shows spike in errors for 3 customers on EU region — several known enterprise routes. Many reports are timeouts and partial responses. I've opened tickets and flagged enterprise SLA customers.

maya: mitigation options: 1) immediately throttle v5 routes to 10% traffic, 2) rollback canary to v4, 3) attempt emergency quota increase with cloud ops, 4) evict noncritical background jobs from GPUs. I can implement 1+4 now. prefer rollback if quota increase won't be instantaneous.

liam: we should also disable KV-cache prewarm for v5 to avoid the big warmup bursts — that's a config flip on runtime. but rollback is safest to restore capacity.

maya: doing quick throttle and disabling prewarm.

maya: /runbook apply-route-config --route v5 --traffic 0.10 --disable-kvcache-prewarm true

ops-bridge-bot: Command executed by maya at 2026-03-15T01:12:20Z: applied traffic=10% to route v5, kvcache prewarm disabled.

samir: autoscaler attempts continue but cloud API responds with 429s for quota. I'll open cloud support ticket now and request emergency quota bump.

samir: open ticket id CLOUD-98765 -> requested +4 GPUs in eu-west-1 for 30m emergency. ETA ~ 45-60m per cloud support.

liam: rolling back canary to v4 now to reduce per-request GPU time. will cut canary to 0% and route back to v4 stable.

maya: please paste rollback command.

liam: `deployctl rollout cancel --model v5 --env hosted && deployctl promote --model v4 --env hosted --routes "v5"`

ops-bridge-bot: liam executed deployctl commands at 2026-03-15T01:24:03Z: v5 canary traffic drained, v4 promoted for affected routes.

maya: metrics now — queue length dropping from 32k -> 7k within 6m, p95 latency improving. partial customer errors still present as queued requests drain.

support-anna: updating customer tickets: ETA for full service restoration ~30-45m. notifying impacted customers that canary rollback in progress and mitigation steps in place.

jess: thanks — we should prepare copy for enterprise comms. tag me if any SLA exposures.

samir: cloud support responded: quota bump will take ~50m. we've also requested a temporary increase to our pool max; pending.

maya: handoff: I'm out at 01:35 UTC for sleep window. handing incident to liam (next oncall). liam — summary: v5 canary caused higher median tokens and KV-cache warmups -> GPU time per req increased -> autoscaler hit region quota and pool max -> queue growth and throttles. Mitigations done: throttled v5 to 10%, disabled kvcache prewarm, rolled back canary to v4, requested quota bump, evicted low-priority background jobs.

liam: taking over. will watch queue and autoscaler logs for next hour and coordinate with cloud ops. also filing immediate follow-ups: - add rollout gating for token-length regression - add kvcache warmup gradual ramp - request permanent increase to region quota - add alert for model-level avg tokens crossing threshold.

maya: thanks. created follow-up cards: CARD-4521 (postmortem), CARD-4522 (quota increase tracking), CARD-4523 (rollout gating). assigning owners: liam -> CARD-4521, samir -> CARD-4522, liam+eng-runtime -> CARD-4523.

support-anna: updating tickets & NOC: customers notified. one enterprise customer asked for timeline; gave 2h window and offered status updates.

liam: current state at 01:49 UTC: queue length 1.2k, p95 latency ~380ms, error rate back to baseline for most routes. autoscaler saw one successful scale event after manual eviction freed capacity. cloud quota still pending.

incidents-bot: Incident update: severity P2, duration 2h planned until final verification. Postmortem owner: liam.

liam: after-action notes to capture in postmortem: - root cause: model v5 increased per-request resource usage (longer contexts + heavy kvcache warmups) not accounted in rollout gating. - contributing: autoscaler lacked pre-emptive quota check; pool hard caps prevented emergency scale. - mitigation worked: rollback + throttle + disable prewarm reduced load. - action items: implement model-level resource regression checks, add kvcache incremental warmup, automate route circuit-breakers, petition cloud for higher regional GPU quota.

jess: also add a customer-impact section and timeline for comms. I'll coordinate with support for messaging.

support-anna: closing notes: tracked impacted customers, offered credits where SLA breached, will keep tickets open until final verification.

liam: I'm running the postmortem draft tonight and will share in #postmortems tomorrow. thanks all for quick response. :bow:
